The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for shoppers
Why, in plain words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on account pages sent shoppers into a calculation that likely divides by the number of things they bought this month, and that fails for anyone who has not bought anything yet this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 20m 55s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 37.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 8,253.46 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #543 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for shoppers
Incident: ErrorRateSustained on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 03:10 UTC, not back to normal by 03:30:55 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 9 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:02:42 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:16:31 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 03:30:55 UTC - PR #543, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 03:10 UTC and was not back to normal by 03:30:55 UTC, at least 20 minutes 55 seconds later. 19.1% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 37.0% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 8,253.46 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching on a new monthly spending summary on account pages sent shoppers into a calculation that likely divides by the number of things they bought this month, and that fails for anyone who has not bought anything yet this month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #543, for a person to review and merge. With monthly-spend-feature back on, account pages could keep failing for any shopper who has bought before but not this month.

Impact
at least 20m 55s - since onset, still not back to normal
37.0% - peak error rate
4,824 - requests failed
0.9% to 19.1% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 2.5%)
at least 8,253.46 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page works out the shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing this month's total by the number of purchases made this month, in `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Nothing guards against an empty month, so a shopper who has bought before but not this month raises ZeroDivisionError and their account page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's error rate across all its requests rose far above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above 2.5% averaged over 10m
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 41 occurrences in 49 minutes, 02:40–03:28; # was 0.50% to 37.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 03:13. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:18–03:28
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 22 occurrences in 19 minutes, 03:10–03:28. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:19,03:22,03:28
why 1 Account page requests failed with ZeroDivisionError raised in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error was logged from the minute of onset onward, while before it account pages were logged rendering normally.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 8 occurrences in 23 minutes, 02:47–03:09
why 2 The requests reaching that code were the ones that evaluated monthly-spend-feature as on. Admin switched the flag on at 03:10:18 UTC, and from that minute the service logged it evaluating on for account page requests, alongside the errors.
  Evidence:
    P1 03:10:18 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off # / on # - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 8 minutes, 03:10–03:17; # was 65 to 182, typically 65, highest at 03:17; # was 18 to 135, typically 18, highest at 03:10
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 9 occurrences in 18 minutes, 03:11–03:28. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:19,03:22,03:28
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or other code change setting it off: the change events read back only the flag changes, all replicas ran the same revision, and account pages were logged rendering normally up to the minute before the flag was switched on.
      T8 03:16:56 Investigator Agent: Read back 1 production change
      T27 03:29:27 Investigator Agent: Read back 2 production changes
      T9 03:16:57 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
      Gad41
    Another flag change: apart from this one, the flag provider's history showed no flag change by anyone but Argus.
      T14 03:16:59 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 03:16:59
      T32 03:29:28 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 03:29:28
why 3 With the flag on, the account page divides this month's spend by the number of the shopper's purchases this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- No test or check was seen that ran the monthly-spend-feature path for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. (AI-2)
- The flag was not seen being rolled out in stages, and no automatic halt on rising errors was seen. In the minute it was switched on, most logged account page evaluations already read it as on. (AI-3, AI-4)
- The ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was paged. (AI-5)
- The alert fired 3 minutes 36 seconds later than its evaluation interval, scraping allowance and onset minute account for. The record does not show what took the rest. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 03:10:18 UTC. This enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% to about 32%. | 0.93 | refuted
C2 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at 03:10:18 UTC. Account page requests that evaluate it as on then fail with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. Nothing was deployed and the rollout has converged. Errors follow the flag: they are high in minutes where evaluations show on and fall back to baseline in minutes where they show off. | 0.90 | refuted, as tested for C1

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 03:17:15 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
 | 03:30:55 | Proposed a fix: PR #543 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 03:10 UTC. ErrorRateSustained fired at 03:16:06 UTC, 6 minutes 6 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above 2.5% averaged over 10m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #543 | open
AI-2 | Before a feature flag on io-shop is switched on in production, require tests that run its flag-on path, including for shoppers with no purchases in the current period. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Roll out io-shop feature flags such as monthly-spend-feature in stages, by percentage of traffic, instead of switching them on for all traffic at once. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Halt a flag rollout on io-shop automatically, and turn the flag back off, when the account page error rate climbs after the flag change. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Link the ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Find out what delayed the ErrorRateSustained alert beyond what its evaluation interval, scraping allowance and onset minute account for, and remove that delay. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. To confirm it took effect, check at the service that account page requests log only monthly-spend-feature=off evaluations, with no monthly-spend-feature=on lines from any replica, and that ZeroDivisionError lines from src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stop appearing. Keep it in place until the fault is fixed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | Find out whether switching monthly-spend-feature off reached every replica and every flag evaluation. After the switch-off the service still logged the flag evaluating on in 03:19, 03:22 and 03:28 UTC, and ZeroDivisionError in the same minutes (03:19, 03:22 and 03:28 UTC). Find what kept serving the flag as on, and whether the error level the Mitigation Agent saw came from those minutes or from other errors. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-9 | Before the Mitigation Agent judges a change it made, have it confirm from the service's own logs that the change reached the service. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 53 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute 9 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 14 minutes 49 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #543.
What went wrong
- The alert came 3 minutes 36 seconds later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
- The Mitigation Agent judged the switch-off refuted and switched monthly-spend-feature back on. Yet after the switch-off, ZeroDivisionError was logged only in the minutes when the flag was still logged evaluating on (03:19, 03:22 and 03:28 UTC and 03:19, 03:22 and 03:28 UTC). Switching it back on likely let more account page requests evaluate it as on and reach the failing path. No log from after it was put back on was read.
- Argus counted C2 as already tested by the switch-off and moved to FIXING with nothing further to try. But C2 said the errors followed the flag's evaluations minute by minute, which pointed to the switch-off not having taken hold everywhere rather than to the flag being innocent.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 9 occurrences in 18 minutes, 03:11–03:28. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:19,03:22,03:28
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, average_spend_per_item_this_month computes account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month). bought_this_month is the account's purchases filtered to in_current_month. Any shopper who has bought before but not this month gets an empty list, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. The page runs this code only when use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false, which is why the errors followed monthly-spend-feature. The flag didn't create the fault. It sent ordinary idle shoppers into a divisor that is empty for them.

The change: when nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0. That means "no spend this month", not an error. Shoppers with purchases this month are handled exactly as before. The lifetime figure (average_spend_per_item), render_spend_summary and the request boundary are unchanged. A shopper with no purchase history at all still raises ZeroDivisionError from the lifetime figure when the flag is off, and the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py check for that failure. So nothing is being silenced: only the monthly figure's empty case now gets a defined answer.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gets two new tests. One calls the monthly average directly for a shopper with purchases but none this month. The other renders through render_spend_summary with use_monthly_summary=True, the flag-on path. Both assert 0 is returned. Against the current code, both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: Account pages on io-shop failed for shoppers for {duration}, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. The trouble began when a new monthly spending summary was switched on for account pages. The summary likely divides by the number of things a shopper has bought this month, so it likely breaks for shoppers who have not bought anything yet this month. Argus estimates the incident cost the shop {customer_loss} in takings. No one was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus switched off the new summary's feature flag, but that did not help, so Argus switched it back on. Argus has also proposed a fix, but it is still an unreviewed draft and has not been put into use.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
